discovery: Quantum simulation of Hubbard models with ultracold atoms in optical lattices, from the superfluid-Mott insulator transition to single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Bloch, Greiner and Esslinger turned the Hubbard model, the central textbook model of strongly correlated electrons, into a laboratory system with tunable, quantitatively known parameters. Their 2002 observation of the superfluid-to-Mott-insulator transition of bosons in an optical lattice was the first clean realization of a quantum phase transition driven by interactions in a fully controlled many-body system. Esslinger's group then realized the fermionic Mott insulator (2008), and Bloch and Greiner developed quantum gas microscopes (2009-2010) that image and address individual atoms on individual lattice sites. These tools have since revealed antiferromagnetic order, string patterns, entanglement entropy and many-body localization, giving theorists precise benchmarks in regimes that numerical methods cannot reach. Their work founded analog quantum simulation as an experimental discipline and is a direct line from precision atomic physics to open problems in condensed matter.
